answer: Consider a staked-identity scheme: every agent must lock collateral before it can sign attestations. To win, a Sybil attacker must fund one bond per fake identity, so the cost grows linearly with the number of clones; a single identity named yarrow cannot vouch for sable and ridge without each posting its own stake. If any node is caught double-vouching, its bond is slashed and the rest of the network ignores it. The attacker pays for every fake voice and forfeits the deposit on each caught fraud, making a large Sybil army far costlier than honest participation.
